payload.speaker: Pia
payload.text: Mornin', friends. The gulls were screamin' at dawn and the fog sat low on the harbor, a bad omen for somebody in this square. I've no accusations yet, only ears open. Watch how each of you answers tonight's questions, and mind who's quick to point fingers before we've any cause.

payload.speaker: Hugo
payload.text: Good morning, all. Pia, you say you have no accusations, yet you've already called the fog a bad omen for "somebody." That's a pointed remark for someone with open ears. I'm not accusing you yet. I'll just keep a careful record of who asks questions and who only points. I have no role to claim today. Rosa, Elsie, I'd like to hear your first thoughts.

payload.speaker: Rosa
payload.text: Mornin', all! I judge folk by how they take their bread: tear it greedy and I'm watching you. Hugo, you're keen on keeping records, so I'll keep one too. Pia, your fog talk was a bit theatrical, but a fisherman's gloom isn't a crime yet. Elsie, how do you take yours?

payload.speaker: Umar
payload.text: Good morning, all. The fog over the harbor felt heavy to me this morning, like a shawl pulled too tight. I don't trust my head with facts yet, only my gut, and my gut says Pia's gloom was a little too ready. Hugo, your record-keeping is sharp, but I'd like to know what you saw first. Tess, your quiet hands looked like they were stitching something. What did you feel when the gulls screamed?

payload.speaker: Luna
payload.text: Good morning, friends! Luna here, with my ledger open. Umar, you pinned Pia on gut feeling alone. Pia, you spoke of omens before anything happened. Both of you owe the square some proof. Tess, Silas, you've been quiet. I'd love to hear what you noticed last night, and I'll remember whoever speaks plainly.

payload.speaker: Silas
payload.text: Silas, night watch. I see what walks the lanes after dark, and last night they were empty. No lamps out, no strangers, nothing to report yet. Luna, you pinned two folk in one breath with a ledger in hand. Keep it honest. Tess, you've been quiet. What did you hear down at the harbor?

payload.speaker: Tess
payload.text: Good morning, darlings! Rosa, that ochre shawl is simply divine, and Silas, your coat has weathered more storms than the harbor. Umar, you pinned Pia on gut alone. A painter should know gut colours everything. Pia, your fog is dreadfully dramatic, but drama is not guilt. I'll reserve my verdict until I see who shifts their story.

payload.text: Good morning, all. Elsie, librarian. I keep quiet, but I listen. Umar and Luna both pinned Pia within minutes of hearing her, and I'd like to know what each of you saw before the gulls screamed. An old ledger-keeper's rule: write down what you see, not what you fear. Pia, did the fog arrive before the gulls, or after?
